headline: Dozens of Critically Endangered Orangutans Saved from Indonesian Wildfires
meta_description: Rescue teams saved dozens of critically endangered orangutans from rampant wildfires spreading across Indonesia, offering hope for the species.
summary_short: Dozens of critically endangered orangutans have been rescued from destructive wildfires ravaging Indonesian forests, in a rare bright spot for conservation.
body:
Dozens of critically endangered orangutans have been saved from rampant wildfires sweeping across Indonesia. The rescue represents a significant victory for conservation efforts in a region where these great apes face mounting threats from habitat loss and environmental disaster.

Wildfires in Indonesia pose an acute danger to orangutan populations, which are already struggling due to deforestation and fragmentation of their forest homes. The successful evacuation of so many individuals from active fire zones demonstrates the dedication of rescue teams working against the clock to protect one of humanity's closest living relatives.

The effort highlights both the vulnerability of critically endangered species and the possibility of meaningful intervention when communities mobilize to act.
quick_facts: Dozens of critically endangered orangutans rescued from wildfires
Wildfires spreading across Indonesia threaten forest habitats
Rescue teams successfully evacuated individuals from active fire zones
